newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Fortis seals MeesPierson buy from ABN AMRO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Fortis seals MeesPierson buy from ABN AMRO.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis said on Friday it sealed the takeover of investment bank MeesPierson from Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV for 2.5 billion guilders ($1.43 billion).
It said the acquisition, which makes it the fourth largest bank in The Netherlands, would make a positive contribution to earnings per share from 1997 for both parent companies.
Fortis, jointly owned by Dutch Fortis Amev and Belgium's Fortis AG, sees the MeesPierson buy as a significant strategic step, offering attractive opportunities in growth markets.
"After due diligence, further talks with the management of MeesPierson and the usual negotiations, agreement has now been reached on price and the other conditions," Fortis said.
"It is our biggest acquisition in The Netherlands so far," Fortis co-chairman Hans Bartelds told a news conference.
"MeesPierson no longer has to compete with its parent."
Fortis Amev and Fortis AG will split the costs of the acquistion, with the Dutch part paying from its own resources and the Belgian parent mulling a rights issue, Bartelds said.
"But a decision on how big the issue might be has not yet been taken," he added.
Fortis had been on the lookout to expand in merchant banking and asset management since it failed to buy Credit Bank Lyonnais Nederland over a year ago.
Fortis and ABN AMRO signalled the deal on October 4 when they signed a letter of intent.
Fortis, which expects the European Commission and relevant authorities to approve the deal in the first quarter of 1997, said MeesPierson would be incorporated in its results over 1997.
The purchase price was in line with analysts' expectations.

MeesPierson, created through the 1993 merger of Mees & Hope with Pierson, Heldring and Pierson, has about 4,000 staff around the world, including Europe, the Far East and United States, and more than 50 billion guilders of assets under management.
It had 1995 operating profit of 182 million guilders and a net profit of 250 million guilders.
The sale ends a business overlap within ABN AMRO, which has expanded into investment banking in recent years, bringing these new operations into competition with MeesPierson itself.
MeesPierson chairman Joost Kuiper said it had been frustrating for MeesPierson staff to work under the ABN AMRO umbrella as there had been competition between the two.

In Amsterdam, Fortis Amev shares gained 0.30 guilders to 58.10 guilders by mid-afternoon, while Fortis AG stock gained 135 Belgian francs to 4,985 each. ABN AMRO advanced 1.90 guilders to 110.80. ($=1.748 guilders)
